newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Central bank says NCDs unrelated to Taiwan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Central bank says NCDs unrelated to Taiwan stocks.

text.p: Taiwan's deputy central bank governor Liang Cheng-chin on Wednesday denied that the bank's repeated issues of negotiable certificates of deposit were aimed at cooling the island's surging stock market.
"The scale of the central bank's NCD issuance was determined by the liquidity situation. It has no direct or close relation with the stock market's movements," Liang told reporters.
"It will not issue more and fewer NCDs simply because the stock market rises or falls," Liang said.
Liang said banking system's liquidity remains fairly loose, prompting the central bank to mop up excess funds.
But the central bank's non-stop NCD issues in recent days were widely seen as aiming to keep a lid on the loose liquidity that many experts say has been fuelling the sizzling stock market rally.
The central bank issued T$10 billion in NCDs on Wednesday, the highest in value since the central bank began its current round of issues on March 3. The issue was the fifth in five days.
Taiwan share prices suffered their first loss in more than a week on Wednesday, losing 84.68 points or 0.99 percent to close at 8,441.52.
The market's benchmark index has gained some 22 percent in 1997 alone and more than 70 percent in the past 12 months.
Whether the linkage is intended or not, the central bank's issuance of short-term paper has been taken by stock market investors as grounds for caution.

"Reported plans by the government to cool down the bourse weakened market sentiment. Investors also were discouraged by the central bank action to repeatedly mop up excess funds," said George Hou, fund manager of Jardine Fleming.
